# Purpose

This document explains `sales_import.R`, an illustrative script that reads and displays a synthetic sales table. It demonstrates clear R documentation without presenting final analytical calculations. The script and its rendered output were reviewed in RStudio on November 17, 2026.

## Inputs

`synthetic_sales.csv` must be in the project working directory.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| month | Character | Fictional month label |
| sales | Numeric | Fictional sales amount in CAD |

The file contains no real store, customer, or personal records.

## Dependencies

The script uses base R. Knitting this document also requires `rmarkdown` and Pandoc. Run knitting from the extracted project directory so relative paths resolve correctly.

## Script walkthrough

### Import the input

The following example shows the import operation. It is displayed for explanation and is not run twice.

```{r import-example, eval=FALSE}
sales <- read.csv("synthetic_sales.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

### Validate and display

The script checks the column names and types before printing the records. This chunk runs the actual script, keeping the documentation tied to its behavior.

```{r run-script, echo=TRUE}
source("sales_import.R", local = knitr::knit_global())
```

## Outputs

The knitted document should show the imported table beneath the execution chunk. The script creates an in-memory object named `sales` and prints its records. It does not write output files or calculate totals.

## Verification

The script ran successfully in RStudio and the document was knitted to HTML. The displayed January–April records matched those shown in the Console. A blank line was inserted before the Purpose heading to correct its formatting. Verification.md records the observed checks.
